title: Rigging Techniques, Procedures, and Applications
author: US Army (FM 5-125, with Change 1)
rights: A work of the US government, in the public domain.
made_from: the Army field manual FM 5-125 (3 October 1995, with Change 1 of 23 February 2001), as published by the US Marine Corps as MCRP 3-17.7J at marines.mil. Chapter 2 is also in the Kiwix pack A Library of Knots
about: The Army's manual on rope and rigging. It covers choosing and caring for rope, and tying knots, hitches, lashings and splices. It also covers rigging hoists, anchors, guy lines and scaffolds to lift, pull and hold loads. Find the knot you need in the pictures below, or start with rope itself.

rights: A work of the US government, in the public domain.

sources.title: Guide 5. Poultry, Red Meats, and Seafoods

made_from: the eight PDFs of the USDA Complete Guide to Home Canning (2015) published by the National Center for Home Food Preservation at nchfp.uga.edu. Guide 6 is also in the Kiwix pack Food for Preppers
about: The US Department of Agriculture's tested guide to canning food at home. It begins with what keeps canned food safe, then gives recipes for fruit, tomatoes, vegetables, meat and seafood, pickles, and jams and jellies. Follow a recipe's method and times exactly: they were tested to prevent botulism.

rights: Published in 1935 with no copyright notice: in the public domain in the United States.

contents: Recipes That Were Popular When the Club Was Founded

notice: This book was published in 1935, and it includes racist caricatures in its dialect verse, sayings and drawings. They were wrong then and are wrong now. Granger presents the book as it was printed, because cutting them would pretend this history did not happen. We don't condone it, and we don't censor it.
about: A Richmond women's club cookbook of 1935: recipes popular in early Virginia, then the club's own, from drinks and soups to breads, preserves, cakes and candies. Start with a section below, or use the contents.
